MathTex.check: Glyphs: a formula the lettering snapshot does not hold fails every command

Mobject.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

Scene.check: Seek, Trace, Hold, Last frame: every scenario is played and seeked; a seeked frame or trace that differs from the played one, a picture that changes after its caption's hold begins, or a step that ends on a different picture from its last frame, fails

Text.check: Text, Legibility, Glyphs: native text that overlaps other text, reads under 14 px at 1280 px, or has characters the fonts cannot draw fails

Transform.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

TransformMatchingShapes.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

TransformMatchingText.check: Motion: a part that pops, cuts in or out, or teleports fails

matchByKey.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

Diagram.check: Routes over labels, Legibility: an imported connector over label ink, or an imported label under 14 px in its viewport, fails

stage.check: Words, Step change: a kept drawing with no text and no describe, or a step whose resting picture equals the previous step's, fails

having.check: Views: a draw that reads a state of another shape throws, which counts as reading its state, so a draw that narrows with having is held to the state it draws

Machine.check: Machines: every state its events reach is drawn and fails if it collides, has a label under 14 px, has no description, does not show its state or is described like another

View.check: Views: at the end of every step, a view whose words, parts, boxes or opacity differ from a fresh draw of the state, placed where a sync would put it, fails

refuse.check: Machines: a bound that stops an event the model refuses anyway fails

view.check: Views: at the end of every step, a view whose words, parts, boxes or opacity differ from a fresh draw of the state, placed where a sync would put it, fails

card.check: Views: a card drawn from state is compared part by part, its lit row included, with a fresh draw

code.check: Views: a code panel drawn from state is compared part by part, its lit bar included, with a fresh draw

keyed.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

keyedParts.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

legend.check: Looks: a caption or line naming a colour or pattern that no word on the stage says fails; a legend that keys the look answers it

table.check: Keys: two parts on the stage with one key at the end of a step fail

depthOrder.check: Invariants: registered with addInvariant, it fails on the first frame that draws a piece out of depth order

DomSink.tooling: a host page that plays a scene into its own live SVG element, as the player's zoom view does (docs/SCENE-OUTPUTS.md)

NullSink.tooling: a test or tool that runs a scene for its state, steps or invariants and draws nothing (the recipes, rayner check)

SeekSink.tooling: a host page or tool that seeks a scene to one time without drawing the frames before it, as the player does

SnapshotSink.tooling: a tool that keeps one SVG frame at a chosen time, such as a contact sheet or a page's still (the render recipe)

StopScene.tooling: a host page or tool with its own sink, which throws it to stop a run and must rethrow it from a catch

StringSink.tooling: a tool that collects every frame of a run as SVG strings (the render recipe)

indexScene.tooling: a host page or tool that lists a scene's steps with their start and end times before seeking (the render recipe)

renderAt.tooling: a host page or tool that draws the scene at one time or step as SVG (the render and document recipes)

renderFrame.tooling: a host page or tool that draws a step's resting picture, or any frame, by the frame number a trace records (the player, the build's poster and rayner check's seeks)

renderElements.tooling: a tool that reads a frame as element records, with each part's box, paint and text (the render recipe)

renderText.tooling: a tool or test that prints a frame as a text drawing, for a terminal or a reviewer (the render recipe)

stepTime.tooling: a host page or tool that finds the time a named step starts or rests at (the render recipe)

toSvgString.tooling: a host page or tool that serializes the scene's current picture as one SVG document

InvariantSink.tooling: an author's test that checks every frame of a run against the scene's invariants (the invariants recipe)

MotionSink.tooling: an author's test that records every frame's motion events, to look for pops, cuts and teleports

TraceSink.tooling: an author's test or tool that records each step's timing, state and evidence while it runs a scene its own way

analyzeMotion.tooling: an author's test that reads recorded motion for pops, cuts and teleports, as rayner check does

bindSnapshots.tooling: an author's test or tool that runs a scene with diagrams outside the command, from its pinned snapshots

describeExplainer.tooling: an author's tool or agent that reads the explainer as one JSON object: scenarios, steps, state and pictures in words

diagramFindings.tooling: an author's test that reads the verifier's warnings on a pinned diagram snapshot without building its diagram

jsonObject.tooling: an author's test or tool that validates and clones state under the trace's JSON rules (the document recipe)

loadFonts.tooling: an author's test or tool that draws text outside a scene's run, and so loads the embedded fonts first

loadProject.tooling: an author's test that runs every scenario of an explainer from its folder, with its script's intent and pinned snapshots, as the command does

loadSnapshots.tooling: an author's test or tool that reads an explainer's pinned diagram snapshots from its folder, to build or inspect one diagram

machinesOf.tooling: an author's test that drives or explores a scene's machines from outside the scene

perf.tooling: an author profiling a scene or a tool: counters, spans and a trace-event export

pictureWordsAt.tooling: an author's test that reads what a reader who cannot see the stage is told about a step's picture

scenarioName.tooling: an author's test or tool that names a scenario the way the command and the player do

scenariosOf.tooling: an author's test or tool that runs every scenario of a scene's settings

stillFrame.tooling: an author's test that reads where a step's picture stops changing, held or not, from its trace

takeMissingGlyphs.tooling: an author's test or tool that draws text outside the command and fails on characters drawn with no glyph

traceScene.tooling: an author's test that compares a run's steps and state with the model (the render and document recipes)

viewMismatch.tooling: an author's test that asks whether a view shows the state it claims, as the Views check does

withIntent.tooling: an author's test that runs a scene directly with its script's intent adopted, as the command runs it

withSettings.tooling: an author's test or tool that runs a scene in one scenario of its settings

features.uses: `TransformMatchingText`, `TransformMatchingShapes` (`shapeKey()`), `TransformMatching` with your own key or `matchByKey()` (keyed components); `summary()`, `pairs`, `removed`, `added`
`new TransformDiff(before, after, { hunks })` and its `plan`; `diffLines`, `parseUnifiedDiff` for hunks

examples.explaining: Two algorithms or policies on the same input
examples.shows: One card with a column per policy, read from the model's trace; one scenario that favours each policy; captions tested against the model

examples.explaining: A code change and what it does to a system
examples.shows: `TransformDiff` on the code, the same edit replayed on the diagram with `ops`, a setting for hit or miss

examples.explaining: Authoring feature reference
examples.shows: Choose a feature scenario: the recipe step shows the author-written API, the result step runs it. See [scope and specialized APIs](../../docs/FEATURE-TOUR.md)

examples.explaining: A protocol or request flow
examples.shows: A sequence diagram revealed message by message (`build: 'frame'`, `reveal`); a setting that adds the attacker's step

examples.explaining: A sequence of separate pictures, one per step

examples.explaining: A data structure changing step by step

examples.explaining: A state machine
examples.shows: A state diagram driven by the real reducer as a `Machine`, code spans boxed from the row it read

examples.explaining: A model the reader could drive with events

examples.explaining: Nested or parallel states

examples.explaining: A race or ordering bug

examples.explaining: A rate or a model's numbers over time

examples.explaining: Identity, hashing or text that changes
